questions.question: What is the official service maintained by W3C to verify HTML document correctness?
questions.explanation: The W3C Nu HTML Validator checks HTML documents against official HTML5 grammar specifications.

questions.question: Why might a webpage render identically in Chrome but fail in Safari if HTML validation errors exist?
options: Different browsers run on different electrical voltages
Each browser's layout engine has different error-recovery algorithms for broken markup
questions.explanation: When HTML is malformed, browsers use different error-correction rules, leading to unpredictable cross-browser visual bugs.

questions.question: Which of the following causes an HTML validation error?
options: Having two elements with the same id attribute value on the same page
questions.explanation: The 'id' attribute must be unique across the document; duplicate IDs trigger validation errors.

questions.question: How do you inspect the live, active DOM tree after JavaScript has executed?
options: Open browser Developer Tools -> Elements panel
Save the webpage as a PDF
questions.explanation: The DevTools Elements tab displays the live, active DOM tree reflecting all JavaScript DOM manipulations.

questions.question: Which legacy presentational element is obsolete and flags an error in modern HTML5 validation?
questions.hint: <center> was deprecated in favor of CSS.
questions.explanation: <center> is obsolete in HTML5; text centering must be achieved using CSS text-align: center.
